rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and acknowledges limits of a single image, but it overstates confidence in expansion/early hatching and describes ICM/TE detail that is only partly discernible in this frame.
Thoroughly integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, prior live birth, male factor, semen parameters, BMI, lifestyle, and endometrial thickness with embryo morphology and prognosis.

Reasoning is clear and mostly consistent, especially emphasizing age-related aneuploidy as the main limiter; minor issues include speculative comments about stimulation effects and some tension between morphology description and exact stage labeling.

Much of the embryo grading discussion is aligned with Gardner principles, but recommending elective double embryo transfer at age 40 with a good blastocyst is not broadly guideline-concordant and weakens overall alignment.

Provides practical transfer and future-cycle recommendations, including counseling, luteal support, uterine review, and consideration of PGT-A; slightly reduced by inclusion of less standard suggestions and some generic advice.
